newsitem.title: USA: Pena resigns as U.S. Transportation Secretary.
newsitem.headline: Pena resigns as U.S. Transportation Secretary.

text.p: U.S. Transportation Secretary Federico Pena said he had formally submitted his resignation to President Bill Clinton at a White House meeting on Tuesday.
In a written statement, Pena officially confirmed what had been reported for the past week -- that he had decided not to stay on in Clinton's second administration.
"This afternoon I met with President Clinton and told him that with a deep sense of pride in our accomplishments these past four years, I have chosen not to serve another term," he said.
Pena said the president thanked him for his "excellent service" and hoped to express his gratitute at a formal occasion.
"Four years ago when I came to office, I had decided to serve only one term," the secretary said. "After 16 years of public service, it's time for me to find new challenges in the private sector."

Pena drew fire for a statement made in May after the crash of a ValuJet airliner near Miami that Valujet was a safe airline. U.S. authorities later grounded ValuJet for safety shortcomings, although it has since resumed flying.
Department officials noted that during Pena's tenure he approved regulations to upgrade the safety levels of small commuter aircraft up to those of large airliners.
In addition, they said, he signed 40 aviation agreements to reduce restrictions on international air travel.
The officials said that during Pena's time in office, U.S. investment in transportation infrastructure increased by 22 percent over the previous four-year period.
